sn12.20:1.2: The Exalted One said:—“I will teach you, Monks, both causal happening and things as having causally happened.
sn12.20:1.3: Hear this, give your mind thoroughly, I will speak.”
sn12.20:1.4: “Even so, lord,” those Monks made response to the Exalted One.
sn12.20:2.2: Conditioned by rebirth is decay and death.
sn12.20:2.3: Whether, Monks, there be an arising of Tathagatas, or whether there be no such arising, this nature of things just stands, this causal status, this causal orderliness, the relatedness of this to that.
sn12.20:2.4: Concerning that the Tathagata is fully enlightened, that he fully understands.
sn12.20:2.5: Fully enlightened, fully understanding, he declares it, teaches it, reveals it, sets it forth, manifests, explains, makes it plain,
sn12.20:2.7: Conditioned by rebirth is decay and death.’
sn12.20:3.7: conditioned by name and shape is sense …
sn12.20:3.8: conditioned by consciousness is name and shape …
sn12.20:3.11: Whether, Monks, there be an arising of Tathagatas, or whether there be no such arising, in each this nature of things just stands, this causal status, this causal orderliness, the relatedness of this to that.
sn12.20:3.12: Concerning that the Tathagata is fully enlightened, that he fully understands.
sn12.20:3.13: Fully enlightened, fully understanding, he declares it, teaches it, reveals it, sets it forth, manifests, explains, makes it plain,
sn12.20:3.15: Conditioned by this, that comes to be.’
sn12.20:3.16: Thus, Monks, that which here is such, not else, not otherwise, the relatedness of this to that:—
sn12.20:3.17: this, Monks, is called causal happening.
sn12.20:4.1: And what, Monks, are things as having causally happened?
sn12.20:4.2: Decay-and-death is impermanent, conditioned, arisen causally, is by nature withering away, passing away, fading away, coming to an end.
sn12.20:4.13: ignorance. These also are impermanent, conditioned, arisen causally, are by nature withering away, passing away, fading away, coming to an end.
sn12.20:4.14: These, Monks, are called things as having causally happened.
sn12.20:5.1: Now inasmuch, Monks, as the Ariyan disciple has by right insight well seen even as they really are both this causal happening and things as having causally happened, never doth it arise, that such as he will run back to the past, thinking:
sn12.20:5.2: ‘Did I live in times gone by? Or did I not? What was I in times gone by? How was I then? Or from being what did I become what?’
sn12.20:5.3: Or that he will run towards the times to come, thinking:
sn12.20:5.4: ‘Shall I be reborn in a future time, or shall I not? What shall I become in the future? How shall I become in the future? Or, being what, shall I in the future become what?’
sn12.20:5.5: Or that he will now become perplexed within himself as to the present day, thinking:
sn12.20:5.6: ‘Am I indeed? Or am I not indeed? What indeed am I? How indeed am I? This person that is I, whence came he, whither will he go?’
sn12.20:5.9: In that the Ariyan disciple, Monks, has by right insight well seen even as they really are both this causal happening and things as having causally happened.”
